Scientific Analysis — Method E:
Method E (Illumination Offset-Normalized Differencing): Directly compensates for the multi-year atmospheric and solar elevation shift by subtracting the per-channel mean difference (ΔR = −36.53, ΔG = −36.17, ΔB = −36.76 DN) prior to differencing (|ΔI| ≥ 40). This centers the static background near zero, collapsing false positives from 52,140 down to just 148 pixels (a 99.72% reduction) while preserving 2,403 true positives. Method E achieves the highest accuracy of all evaluated methods: Precision = 0.9420, Specificity = 0.9975, IoU = 0.3462, and Dice = 0.5143.
